question: Where do funded settlement and public verification spend their time, and what can be removed without changing any circuit, proof, statement, verifying key or signing rule?
finding: Halo2 Params::new(17) (the fixed IPA commitment parameters on Vesta) takes about 87 s here and was rebuilt from scratch every time a process needed it: once for the payout proving key, once when the MPC gate re-verifies the six payout proofs, once in the SDK's independent replay before FROST signing, and once in every public verification. It is deterministic.

change.summary: crates/output-binding fixed_params(): the serialized parameters' SHA-256 is pinned in the source (PARAMS_SHA256). A cached copy is used only if its bytes hash to that digest, so it is the same value as recomputing; otherwise the parameters are recomputed in memory, checked against the same digest (a mismatch is an error) and the cache is rewritten when its location is writable. All five K=17 uses (proving key, set verification, single-row checks) go through it.
change.cache_location: DARKCALL_HALO2_PARAMS, else .local/cache/halo2-vesta-k17.params. The hosted image computes it at build time into /src/params (outside the .local volume that compose mounts) and leaves it read-only to the app user.
change.unchanged: circuits, K, verifying keys (still derived by keygen_vk from the circuit), proofs and their bytes, public statements, row hashes, signing rules, and every verification step. Nothing is skipped: the payout proofs are still re-verified by the MPC gate, by the SDK before FROST signing, and by the public verifier.

public_verification_same_bundle.method: run back to back; 'recomputed' points DARKCALL_HALO2_PARAMS at an unwritable path, so every use recomputes as before the change

funded_settlement_one_unit_regtest.conditions: Same binaries for both runs, same auction terms (1 unit, reserve 20, budget 100), same sealed demo bids 77, 61, 43, 21, driven over HTTP by scripts/check_fresh_settlement.py on the isolated NU7 regtest node; RAYON_NUM_THREADS=2; one row worker. The 'recomputed' run's server had DARKCALL_HALO2_PARAMS pointing at an unwritable path; the 'cached' run's server pointed it at a read-only copy (file 444, directory 555), as in the hosted image, with the default cache moved aside: it was not recreated, so every stage read the read-only copy.
funded_settlement_one_unit_regtest.not_a_controlled_benchmark: Shared 16 GiB M1 with heavy swap in use and another project's node running. During the recomputed run, a nice'd cargo test build overlapped for about a minute around 13:47 (payout rows 3-4). Payout row proving does not touch the parameter generation, yet it ran 678 s in the first run and 467 s in the second: that difference is machine load, not the cache, and is not claimed.
funded_settlement_one_unit_regtest.attributed_to_the_cache: 251 s (4.2 min) per settlement, from the three stages that build the parameters; public verification 106 s to 18 s for this bundle. The rest of the 464 s driver difference is machine load.
funded_settlement_one_unit_regtest.same_results: Both: price 61, 1 sold, two confirmations, own receipts won 39 / lost 100 / 100 / 100, six payout proofs verified before signing and again publicly, tamper refused before key read, foreign capability refused, settle before clear refused, clear and settle before funding refused (400), a concurrent settle refused (409) while the recorded check still answered.

cross_verification.checks: native row proofs, C++ auction proof, accepted book and recipients, transaction outputs, native proofs and signatures

cache_safety.unit_test: cached_params_equal_recomputed_ones_and_fail_closed (k = 4): a miss computes, checks and writes; a hit returns identical bytes; one flipped byte, a truncated file, valid k = 5 parameters and k = 5 cut to the k = 4 size are all ignored, recomputed and replaced; a pinned digest that recomputation does not reproduce is an error
cache_safety.pinned_digest_at_k17: a fresh Params::new(17) serialized to the pinned digest; the cache read back byte-identical
cache_safety.corrupt_read_only_cache: one flipped byte in a read-only file (444) in a read-only directory (555): --prepare-params recomputed (82.6 s, params_already_cached false); a public verification of testnet-one-unit-nu7-v1 with that cache passed every check in 106 s, using parameters recomputed in memory; the file's hash was unchanged and no other cache was written. The corrupt bytes are never used and the check does not stop.

parallel_payout_rows.what: DARKCALL_ROW_WORKERS (1, 2, 3 or 6; default 1) lets a fresh funded settlement prove its six payout rows several at a time with the warm worker's prove_rows and the same fixed verification per row. More than one passes the existing Linux memory guard (8 GiB total plus 8 GiB per worker, 8 GiB available per worker), checked by settle_fresh_book.py's preflight (darkcall-native-gate --row-capacity) before any deposit and again before the key is built. A resumed settlement with existing proofs keeps the one-at-a-time path.
parallel_payout_rows.this_machine: refused for 2, 3 and 6 (not Linux); 1 is the unchanged default

warm_worker_not_integrated: After the cache, building the payout key takes 28 s. A long-lived worker that keeps the proving key resident would save at most that per settlement, while holding the key in memory on a shared host; it was not wired into funded settlement.
